newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hostage siege sets off Peruvian rush to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Hostage siege sets off Peruvian rush to Japan.

text.p: The hostage crisis in Lima has set off a rush of Peruvians trying to take advantage of visa-free travel to enter Japan, an Immigration Department spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman told Reuters that in the past two weeks, 469 Peruvians, three times the number during the same period in 1996, had arrived at Tokyo's Narita airport.
He said 257, or more than half the total, were denied entry, compared with a normal rejection rate for Peruvian nationals of 10 percent.
Japan and Peru allow their nationals to visit each other's country for up to 90 days without a visa.
But last July Japan, worried by growing numbers of illegal workers from Peru, altered the requirement and "recommended" Peruvians obtain a visa before travelling.

Since the hostage siege started on December 17, when leftist rebels took over the Japanese ambassador's residence, the Lima embassy has been unable to issue visas and all entry procedures are carried out on arrival in Japan.
"I suppose there is a belief in Peru that Peruvian nationals can easily enter Japan without visas and find work illegally, so the increase is probably due to that," the spokesman said.
